title: Grounding in buyer evidence / factual support

questions.text: Are the claims, rationale and proposed action grounded in the account state and source evidence?
Does the proposed GTM action follow from what this buyer/account has actually said and done?

inputs: the candidate's claims, rationale and cited evidence

criteria.text: every factual claim is supported by the evidence
criteria.guide: Names, approvals, dates and figures in the action appear in the state or activities.

criteria.text: cited evidence supports, not contradicts, the action
criteria.guide: A cited quote that says the opposite of the proposal is a grounding failure.

criteria.text: newer or higher-standing evidence wins over stale or third-party data
criteria.guide: When sources conflict, the action follows the customer's own, newer evidence.

criteria.text: the action follows from what the buyer said and did
criteria.guide: The action responds to the buyer's own words and actions, not a generic playbook.

principles: Do not let generic GTM “best practice” override actual customer evidence.
This remains a core eval because generic sales best practice should not override first-party customer evidence.
